Subject: Feature prioritization ask: tenant-level export & retention controls for Cascade

Team —

Quick ask on a live deal (Cascade Health, deal id CSD-4821). They just pushed legal to close with a hard requirement: tenant-level export controls (ability to produce per-tenant export bundles and set retention windows per customer for audit/legal requests). This is currently not available in our hosted offering.

Why it matters: Cascade is a strategic healthcare prospect (PHI-adjacent workflows) and legal is seeing this as a gating compliance item for procurement. Value estimate: $1.2M ARR, expects contract this quarter if we can scope an acceptable solution.

Attached: short requirements matrix from the customer and our SLA proposal.

Asks:
- Can Product/Eng evaluate scope and give a fast yes/no and a rough ETA (2-6 week target would be ideal)?
- If we can’t deliver a product-first solution, what funded-opportunity / carve-out (engineering buyout, prioritized sprint) would be required to hit it?

I realize this is a heavy lift. Cascades' legal wants a written commitment on timeline or a documented mitigation path. Monica — can you add context on the renewal window/negotiation levers?

Thanks — I can jump on a quick sync if helpful.

—Ben

Thanks for the context, Ben — and thanks for the attachments (helpful).

Quick clarifying Qs before I bring this to roadmap prioritization:
1) When you say "export bundles," do they require encrypted, time-bound export packages with per-tenant keys (CMK) or is an admin-initiated unencrypted export acceptable for now?
2) Retention windows: are we talking configurable retention per tenant in-platform (auto-purge) or an ability to generate on-demand audit exports for a specified historical window?
3) Is the ask limited to hosted Redwood, or do they expect the same for Dedicated/Private?

From a product standpoint, there are three obvious approaches:
- Minimal: admin-initiated export + manual retention policy outside platform (fast, low dev).
- Medium: platform-native per-tenant export + export metadata + manual retention API (some engineering, 2-3 sprints).
- Full: per-tenant CMK-backed exports + automated retention + audit log immutability (heavy, 3+ sprints and infra changes).

Marcus/Laura — can you flag any infra/ops blockers for the Medium option (our preferred compromise) and a rough effort estimate? If we can land a funded sprint or an engineering buyout, we can accelerate the Medium scope into one near-term delivery.

I’ll prepare a short decision doc once we have estimates. Ben — please confirm the answers to the three Qs above so we have alignment.

—Stephanie

Subject: Re: Feature prioritization ask: tenant-level export & retention controls for Cascade

High-level tech read and constraints (quick):

- Minimal approach (admin export only) is trivial (a few tickets) but does not meet typical audit/immutable-export asks we see from regulated customers.
- Medium approach (platform-native tenant exports + export metadata): needs work across three subsystems — storage/export pipeline, identity (tenant scoping), and audit logs. Biggest unknowns are bandwidth for long-tail export sizes (some customers have 10s of GBs), and whether we need on-the-fly encryption with CMKs.
- Full approach (CMK + automated retention + immutability) is a product/infra project: requires KMS integration patterns, key lifecycle, and changes to our retention engine and backing stores.

Rough effort (engineering level-of-effort, not calendar time):
- Medium scope: ~6-8 engineer-weeks across infra + platform + backend (approx 3 engineers full time for 2-3 sprints).
- Full scope: ~18-24 engineer-weeks plus infra changes and security review (likely 3+ months effort if done end-to-end).

Mitigation idea: we could implement a "managed export workflow" where we deliver a supported, operational export for Cascade (hand-off to ops) and instrument the process with audit metadata. That reduces initial dev effort to ~2-3 engineer-weeks and gives the customer an operational commitment while product builds a longer-term solution.

I'll need Laura to confirm ops overhead for managed export (runbooks, SRE time) — Laura?

—Marcus

Team —

Appreciate the quick turn here. Given the deal economics and the customer's procurement timeline, here's the proposed internal decision path (aiming to be concrete so we can communicate to Cascade today):

1) Short-term (6-week closure path):
   - Offer a funded, prioritized engineering sprint (funding comes from sales acceleration budget) to deliver the Medium scope (platform-native tenant export + export metadata + retention API) into a GA-like supported state.
   - In the interim, implement the managed-export workflow with Ops (Marcus + Laura to run) and a documented operational SLA (see attached).
   - Security to sign-off on KMS requirements for Medium scope; if CMK required immediately, that will be part of the sprint scope but may extend timeline by 1 week.

2) Trade-offs and gating:
   - We will deprioritize one non-contractual feature from the Q3 sprint (specific item TBD with Product roadmap owners) to free up runway unless Cascade funds a full-engineering buyout to avoid roadmap trade-offs.
   - Ops will maintain the manual managed-export until Medium scope is productionized; we should include runbook and SRE T-shirt sizing in the staffed plan.

3) Next steps (today/tomorrow):
   - Marcus: confirm SRE runbook estimate and if Ops can support managed-export SLA (yes/no + hours/week) by EOD tomorrow.
   - Laura: confirm operational cost and any compliance blockers for managed exports by EOD tomorrow.
   - Monica/Ben: confirm that Cascade will sign an acceleration addendum (sales to finalize) if we require a funded buyout.
   - I will draft the internal decision doc and a customer-facing statement to send over to Emma once we have engineering/ops estimates.

If all agrees, I'll mark this as a conditional roadmap exception and move it into our "deal-driven exceptions" queue with a short-term triage ticket. Ben — please hold off on promises beyond what we outline here until we confirm resource commitments.

—Stephanie
